thoughts.t: Every expert you admire started out as a beginner.
Mistakes are proof that you are trying.
Small steps every day add up to big journeys.
Curiosity is a superpower. Keep asking 'why?'
Be the reason someone smiles today.
You do not have to be perfect to be amazing.
Reading a page a day opens a new door every day.
Kind words cost nothing but are worth a lot.
A question is the first step to an answer.
When something feels hard, it means your brain is growing.
Try, learn, try again. That is how everyone gets better.
Your effort today is a gift to your future self.
Listening is the first step to learning.
Help one person today. It will make two people happy: them and you.
It is brave to say, 'I don't know yet.'
Practice does not make perfect. Practice makes progress.
A tidy desk makes room for big ideas.
Every day is a fresh page. Write something good on it.
Be patient with yourself. Seeds take time to grow.
Sharing a smile is the easiest way to make a friend.
Dream big, start small, keep going.
Learning is an adventure with no finish line.
Courage is doing the right thing, even when it is hard.
You can't pour from an empty cup. Rest, eat well and play too.
Say thank you often. Gratitude makes happy days happier.
Different is not wrong. Different is interesting.
Your best is enough, and your best grows every day.
Ask for help. Smart people do it all the time.
A good friend listens, helps and forgives.
Be honest, even when no one is watching.
Water, sunshine and patience grow plants. Practice, rest and patience grow skills.
Every 'wrong answer' teaches you something new.
Look closely. Wonder is hiding everywhere.
Start with what you can do. Then do a little more.
Happiness grows when you share it.
Respect everyone: young, old, and everyone in between.
Big goals are just small goals standing in a line.
Be gentle with animals, plants and people.
Doing your homework is like charging your brain's battery.
Celebrate small wins. They lead to big ones.
A calm breath can turn a bad moment around.
Leave every place a little better than you found it.
Your voice matters. Use it kindly.
Focus on progress, not perfection.
Today is a perfectly good day to begin.
Be a learner, not a knower.
Effort is never wasted. It always teaches you something.
Be kind to yourself. You are still learning.
One good book can be a best friend.
Ideas grow when you share them.
Some days you win. Other days you learn.
Clean water, clean air and clean hearts make a happy world.
Plant a tree, plant a hope.
Questions open doors that answers never could.
The more you learn, the more you can see.
Mistakes are not the end of learning. They are the middle of it.
Be someone who makes others feel welcome.
Fill your mind with good thoughts, your hands with good work and your heart with kindness.
Believe you can learn anything, one step at a time.
Even the tallest tree started as a tiny seed.
Do a little revision every day, and exams won't feel scary.
Being kind is always cool.
Reading is travelling without a ticket.
Nature is the best classroom. Step outside and look around.
Count your blessings, not your problems.
Sleep well, dream big, wake up ready.
Let your light shine so others can find their way.
Being wrong is how we find out what is right.
Every 'no' you hear is one step closer to a 'yes'.
A clear mind starts with a clear morning: water, sunlight, a stretch.
Learning a new word every day adds up to 365 new words a year.
Be the kind of friend you would like to have.
Patience is not waiting. It is staying calm and keeping on.
There is always something to be grateful for.
You become what you practise.
Use your words to build, not to break.
Gentle words are stronger than shouting.
The world needs your ideas.
Today, notice one beautiful thing.
Don't be afraid to stand out.
You can do hard things.
Each sunrise brings a new chance.
Be bold enough to try something new today.
Read, think, wonder, repeat.
The best way to learn something is to teach it.
Water your dreams with hard work.
Good manners open every door.
Do it now. Later can become never.
Believe in yourself, and others will too.
Don't just study to pass. Study to understand.
A healthy body helps a happy mind.
Be thankful for teachers. They plant seeds that grow for a lifetime.
Kindness needs no translation.
Every page you read makes your world bigger.
Small acts of kindness can change someone's whole day.
What you do every day matters more than what you do once in a while.
Ask good questions. They are as valuable as good answers.
It's okay to feel nervous. It means you care.
A positive thought is a seed for a good day.
Help keep your school and street clean. It is everyone's home.
When you share knowledge, you don't lose it. You double it.
Respect your elders, love the young, and be friends with all.
Today's practice is tomorrow's skill.
Think it, try it, test it, improve it.
Every mountain top is reached one step at a time.
Be patient. Even the Moon takes about two weeks to grow from new to full.
Mistakes are like stepping stones, not walls.
Say sorry when you are wrong. It is a sign of strength.
Look at the stars tonight and remember how big the world is.
Every subject is a key to a different door.
Real friends are happy when you succeed.
A focused hour is better than a distracted day.
Choose to be kind, every single time.
You are never too young to make a difference.
Hope is the light that keeps us going.
Learn something new today, and teach it to someone.
Keep your promises, big and small.
When you feel stuck, take a short walk and try again.
Be the first to say hello.
It's not about being the best. It's about being better than you were yesterday.
Your mind is a garden. Plant good ideas.
Happy hearts make happy homes.
Say 'please' and 'thank you'. They are magic words.
Listen more than you speak, and you will learn a lot.
Brave is not 'no fear'. Brave is 'I'll do it anyway'.
Knowledge is a treasure no one can steal.
Small progress is still progress.
A good habit a day keeps the worries away.
Treat others the way you want to be treated.
Be honest. It makes life simple.
Rise, shine and give it your best.
Think like a scientist: ask, guess, test and learn.
Fill your day with curiosity.
You are a work in progress, and that's wonderful.
Help is just a question away.
Laugh often. It's good for your heart.
Clean hands, healthy you.
Every day you learn something, you become a little more you.
Your kindness could be someone's sunshine.
Big dreams need early mornings and steady effort.
The best view comes after the hardest climb.
Be careful with your words. Once said, they can't be taken back.
Make friends with books. They never leave you.
Courage grows when you use it.
Every great invention started with someone asking 'what if?'
Good things take time.
A happy mind learns faster.
Give your best, then let go of the worry.
Today is a good day to be kind.
Each of us is unique, like a fingerprint.
Be proud of how far you've come.
Learning is fun when you're curious.
One kind word can change a day.
Respect nature. We are part of it.
Be a problem-solver, not a problem-finder.
A little progress each day adds up to big results.
Be someone others can trust.
Being different makes the world colourful.
Talk less, do more.
Every expert keeps practising.
Find joy in the little things.
Be bright like the Sun and calm like the Moon.
Courage, kindness and curiosity: carry them everywhere.
Be a friend to someone who is alone today.
Studying with focus for a short time beats studying distracted for a long time.
Your words have power. Use them to lift people up.
Take care of your books, and they will take care of you.
Ideas are like stars. The more you look, the more you see.
Shine bright, stay kind.
Give yourself credit for trying.
A clean room, a clear mind.
Patience and practice can turn the impossible into the possible.
Smile at someone new today.
Every great journey starts with 'let's go'.
Your dreams are worth working for.
Do one thing today that your future self will thank you for.
Mistakes help you find the right path.
Believe in your own spark.
Some of the best lessons are learned outside the classroom.
Knowledge grows when it is used.
Little by little, a little becomes a lot.
Learn to listen, listen to learn.
Ask, explore, discover.
Healthy food, happy body.
Look for the good in others.
Bravery is speaking up for someone who is being treated unfairly.
Great minds discuss ideas.
Today is another chance to get better.
Respect the time of others. Be on time.
Follow your curiosity. It knows the way.
Make learning a habit, not a chore.
Even small candles light up dark rooms.
Every dream needs a plan and a little bit of courage.
Being kind to animals shows a big heart.
Do something creative today: draw, write, build or sing.
Hard work today, happy results tomorrow.
Choose friends who make you better.
A great question can be more powerful than a great answer.
Keep calm and keep learning.
Your effort is your superpower.
Always do your best. What you plant now, you will harvest later.
Be the same person when no one is watching.
Be a voice of encouragement.
Learn the rules well, so you know how to be creative with them.
You are capable of more than you know.
Stay curious, stay kind, stay you.
Planning saves time.
Every day is a learning day.
Help your friends learn. Teaching makes you learn too.
A positive attitude makes hard work feel lighter.
Be like a tree: stay grounded, keep growing, give shade to others.
Every drop of water saved counts.
Big changes begin with small habits.
Courage is saying 'I'll try' when you feel unsure.
Be generous with praise and careful with criticism.
Take a deep breath. You've got this.
Ask questions until you understand.
Your future is bright. Keep shining.
A strong mind needs exercise too: read, think and solve.
Learn to enjoy the journey, not just the destination.
Be grateful for small things, and big things will feel even bigger.
Be honest about what you know, and curious about what you don't.
Patience is a superpower that grows quietly.
Plant kindness and you will grow friendship.
Your best effort is always good enough for today.
Respect is earned by giving it.
One more try might be the one that works.
Practice a skill a little every day, and one day it will feel easy.
Think of three things you are thankful for before you sleep.
Every 'aha!' moment starts with a 'hmm?'
A focused mind is a powerful mind.
Keep your heart open and your mind curious.
Don't give up on something you really want.
Be careful, be kind, be curious.
Practice makes progress.
Where there's a will, there's a way.
Rome wasn't built in a day.
Actions speak louder than words.
Better late than never.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
Slow and steady wins the race.
thoughts.by: Moral of Aesop's fable 'The Tortoise and the Hare'

thoughts.t: Honesty is the best policy.
A friend in need is a friend indeed.
Every cloud has a silver lining.
Two heads are better than one.
Many hands make light work.
The early bird catches the worm.
Knowledge is power.
Fall seven times, stand up eight.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Look before you leap.
United we stand, divided we fall.
Necessity is the mother of invention.
An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
Little strokes fell great oaks.
Well done is better than well said.
Lost time is never found again.
If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
thoughts.by: Isaac Newton, letter to Robert Hooke (1675)

thoughts.t: To know what you know and to know what you do not know: that is true knowledge.
Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high...
बूँद-बूँद से घड़ा भरता है। (Drop by drop, the pot gets filled.)
जहाँ चाह, वहाँ राह। (Where there's a will, there's a way.)
काल करे सो आज कर, आज करे सो अब। (Do tomorrow's work today, and today's work now.)

धीरे-धीरे रे मना, धीरे सब कुछ होय। माली सींचे सौ घड़ा, ऋतु आए फल होय। (Slowly, slowly, O mind, everything happens in its own time. The gardener may pour a hundred pots of water, but fruit comes only in its season.)
ऐसी बानी बोलिए, मन का आपा खोय। औरन को सीतल करै, आपहु सीतल होय। (Speak words that are free of pride; they bring calm to others and to yourself.)
बड़ा हुआ तो क्या हुआ, जैसे पेड़ खजूर। पंथी को छाया नहीं, फल लागे अति दूर। (What use is being big like a date palm, if it gives no shade to travellers and its fruit hangs far out of reach?)
रहिमन धागा प्रेम का, मत तोड़ो चटकाय। टूटे से फिर ना जुड़े, जुड़े गाँठ परि जाय। (Do not snap the thread of love; once broken, it does not join again, and if it does, a knot remains.)
करत-करत अभ्यास के, जड़मति होत सुजान। रसरी आवत जात ते, सिल पर परत निसान। (With steady practice, even a slow learner becomes wise, just as a rope, rubbing again and again, leaves a mark on stone.)
विद्या ददाति विनयम्। (Knowledge gives humility.)
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः। (Work gets done by effort, not by wishing.)
सत्यमेव जयते। (Truth alone triumphs.)
वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्। (The whole world is one family.)
अहिंसा परमो धर्मः। (Non-violence is the highest duty.)
विद्याधनं सर्वधनप्रधानम्। (The wealth of knowledge is the greatest of all wealth.)
अति सर्वत्र वर्जयेत्। (Too much of anything should be avoided.)
मातृदेवो भव। पितृदेवो भव। आचार्यदेवो भव। (Honour your mother, your father and your teacher.)
योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्। (Yoga is skill in action.)
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। (Your right is to your work, not to its results.)
उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत। (Arise, awake, and learn from the wise.)
असतो मा सद्गमय। तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय। (Lead me from untruth to truth, from darkness to light.)
सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः। (May everyone be happy.)
अलसस्य कुतो विद्या? (How can a lazy person gain knowledge?)
परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः। (Good people use their gifts to help others.)
क्षणशः कणशश्चैव विद्यामर्थं च साधयेत्। (Gain knowledge moment by moment, and wealth bit by bit.)
श्रद्धावान् लभते ज्ञानम्। (One who is sincere and devoted gains knowledge.)
Learn well what is worth learning, and then live by what you have learned.
Using harsh words when kind ones are at hand is like picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit is there.
Chance helps the mind that is prepared.
Learning is like rowing a boat upstream: if you stop moving forward, you slip back.
A pencil and a curious mind can go anywhere.
When you don't understand, slow down. Speed comes later.
Your notebook is a map of your learning. Keep it neat.
Try explaining today's lesson to a family member at dinner.
Wonder at the sky, the sea and the tiny ant. All of it is amazing.
A good question is a gift to the whole class.
Bring your full attention, and the lesson will meet you halfway.
There is no shortcut to understanding, but there are many fun roads.
Be proud of your effort, not just your marks.
Drink water, stretch, and then study. Your brain will thank you.
Your handwriting tells a story. Make it a clear one.
Treat every mistake like a clue in a mystery.
Learn one new fact today and share it with a friend.
The night sky is free. Look up and wonder.
Before you give up, try one more way.
Curious minds are never bored.
Respect starts with listening.
Courage means raising your hand even when you're not sure.
Revise today, relax tomorrow.
Every subject you learn makes you a better problem-solver.
A kind deed is never too small.
Grow like a sunflower: always turn towards the light.
Spend some time each day away from screens.
The library is a treasure chest. Open it often.
Be a good loser and a humble winner.
Every sport, game and lesson teaches patience.
Learn to say 'well done' to others. It feels great.
A good morning routine builds a good day.
Write down your goals. Goals on paper feel real.
Today, be kind to someone who is different from you.
Try something you think you're bad at. You might surprise yourself.
Feelings are like weather: they change. Be patient with them.
Your brain loves puzzles. Feed it one today.
Clever is good. Kind and clever is even better.
Rest is part of training, not the opposite of it.
Note down one question you had today. Find its answer tomorrow.
If you finish early, help a friend.
Be patient with people who are learning, just as others are patient with you.
Make your own sunshine on a cloudy day.
Small savings, like small steps, take you far.
Learn the 'why', not just the 'what'.
Mistakes made in practice save you mistakes in the exam.
Stand tall, speak clearly, smile warmly.
Saying 'I can't do it yet' is very different from 'I can't do it'.
Each person you meet knows something you don't.
Pay attention to the little things. They often matter most.
Your future self is cheering for you.
Good habits are like seeds: plant them early.
A healthy breakfast is fuel for a busy brain.
Be gentle with your words and strong in your actions.
Keep a notebook of wonders: things that make you say 'wow'.
Today's struggle is tomorrow's strength.
Celebrate others' success as if it were your own.
Mind your manners online, just as you would face to face.
Learning together is twice the fun.
Be like a river: keep flowing around obstacles.
Ask your grandparents a question about the old days today.
Clear explanations come from clear understanding.
Sometimes the best thing to do is take a deep breath and begin again.
Some lessons take time to sink in. That's normal.
A minute of planning can save an hour of confusion.
The joy of solving a hard problem is worth the effort.
Make someone's day by saying something nice.
Each new skill is a new superpower.
Practise gratitude: name three good things about today.
Every page turned is a step forward.
Speak up for what is fair.
A smile costs nothing and brightens everything.
Be the student who asks 'how does that work?'
Read the question twice, answer once.
Today's small effort is tomorrow's big result.
Big or small, every living thing deserves kindness.
Every map was drawn by someone who explored first.
Listen to the birds in the morning. Nature has its own music.
Each day you choose to learn, you grow a little taller inside.
When you help someone learn, you learn it twice.

wow.t: A group of flamingos is called a 'flamboyance'.
Sharks have been around longer than trees.
From one sunrise to the next, a day on Mercury lasts about 176 Earth days.
Bananas are very slightly radioactive because they contain potassium.
On hot summer days, the iron of the Eiffel Tower expands and the tower can grow up to about 15 cm taller.
Wombats make cube-shaped poop!
A snail's tongue has thousands of tiny teeth.
Koalas have fingerprints that look very much like human fingerprints.
There are more trees on Earth than stars in our Milky Way galaxy.
A teaspoon of material from a neutron star would weigh billions of tonnes on Earth.
On Mars, sunsets look blue.
The Moon is moving away from Earth by about 3.8 cm every year.
More than a million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
A shrimp's heart is in the front part of its body, the part that includes its head.
Starfish have no blood. They pump seawater through their bodies instead.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times a minute.
Polar bears have black skin under their thick fur, and their fur is not really white: each hair is see-through.
Giraffes have seven neck bones, the same number as humans.
Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror.
Crows can remember human faces for years.
Dolphins give each other names: special signature whistles.
A newborn kangaroo is about the size of a jelly bean.
Some turtles can take in oxygen through their bottoms!
Axolotls can regrow lost legs, and even parts of their heart and brain.
Tiny animals called tardigrades have survived being exposed to outer space.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for about 3,800 years.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
Lightning strikes somewhere on Earth dozens of times every second.
At a special temperature and pressure called the 'triple point', water can exist as ice, liquid water and water vapour all at the same time.
Glass is made mostly from sand.
Diamonds can burn, because they are made of carbon.
Your stomach makes a fresh layer of slimy mucus all the time, so its acid does not digest the stomach itself.
Try it: you can't hum while holding your nose closed!
Babies are born without hard kneecaps. They start as soft cartilage and harden later.
Your fingernails grow faster than your toenails.
Your brain uses about 20% of your body's energy, even though it is only about 2% of your weight.
Astronauts can grow a few centimetres taller in space, because their spines stretch without gravity.
On the Moon, you would weigh only about one-sixth of what you weigh on Earth.
Saturn's moon Enceladus shoots jets of water ice into space from an ocean under its crust.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.
The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old, roughly halfway through its life.
Some sand dunes 'sing', making a low booming sound when sand slides down them.
A pineapple plant takes about two years to grow one pineapple.
The tiny dots on the outside of a strawberry are its seeds. Each one is really a tiny fruit with a seed inside.
Apples float in water because about a quarter of an apple is air.
A cashew nut grows hanging from the bottom of a fruit called the cashew apple.
Peanuts grow underground.
Long ago, most carrots were purple or yellow. Orange carrots became popular in the Netherlands in the 1600s.
Coffee beans are really the seeds of a red fruit called a coffee cherry.
The Great Banyan tree in the botanical garden at Howrah, near Kolkata, is so wide that it looks like a whole forest.
The seeds in a sunflower head grow in spirals that follow Fibonacci numbers.
Bees can see ultraviolet light, which we cannot see. Many flowers have hidden UV patterns that guide bees.
Fireflies make light without making heat. It is called 'cold light'.
Some penguins give a pebble to the penguin they want as a mate.
The calls of blue whales can travel hundreds of kilometres under water.
Flamingos are pink because of pigments in the shrimp and algae they eat.
A chameleon's tongue can be longer than its whole body.
Crocodiles cannot stick their tongues out.
Rats make tiny laughing squeaks when they are tickled, too high for us to hear.
Cats spend around 12 to 16 hours a day sleeping.
Each dog's nose print is unique, like a human fingerprint.
Horses can sleep standing up.
Ants don't have lungs. Air enters through tiny holes along their bodies.
Only female mosquitoes bite. They need blood to make eggs.
Weight for weight, spider silk is stronger than steel.
Wood frogs can freeze solid in winter and come back to life when they thaw.
The mantis shrimp punches so fast that it can crack a crab's shell in one hit.
Cheetahs can't roar, but they can purr.
A tiger's skin is striped, not just its fur.
No two zebras have exactly the same stripes.
Goats have rectangular pupils, which help them see danger all around.
Jellyfish were drifting in the oceans long before the dinosaurs.
Most of Earth's fresh water is frozen in ice sheets and glaciers, and most of that ice is in Antarctica.
Mount Everest is still growing by a few millimetres every year.
The Moon always shows the same face to Earth, so we never see its far side from here.
Sound cannot travel through empty space, so space is silent.
Istanbul is a city in two continents: Europe and Asia.
Australia is wider than the Moon.
The Sahara Desert was green, with lakes and hippos, between about 11,000 and 5,000 years ago.
The Atlantic Ocean gets wider by a few centimetres every year.
Oxygen gas is colourless, but liquid oxygen is pale blue.
Breathing helium makes your voice sound squeaky because sound travels faster through it.
When you look at stars, you see light that left them long ago. You are looking into the past!
A single teaspoon of healthy soil can hold hundreds of millions of tiny living things, such as bacteria.
All the blood vessels in one human body, laid end to end, could stretch around Earth more than twice.
Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System.
The first computer mouse, made in the 1960s, had a wooden case.
One of the first webcams was set up at Cambridge University to watch a coffee pot.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed for typewriters in the 1870s.
More than 2,000 years ago, the Indian scholar Pingala described poetic rhythms using a system much like binary numbers.
Snakes and ladders comes from an old Indian game called Moksha Patam.
Ludo comes from the old Indian game Pachisi.
The Iron Pillar in Delhi is about 1,600 years old and has hardly rusted.
Rani ki Vav, a stepwell in Gujarat, has hundreds of carved stone sculptures.
The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved downwards from a single giant rock.
The idea for Velcro came from burrs that stuck to a Swiss inventor's dog.
The microwave oven was invented after Percy Spencer noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket melted near a radar machine.
Louis Braille was only 15 when he created his reading system for the blind.
The ice lolly on a stick was invented by an 11-year-old boy, Frank Epperson.
The sandwich is named after the Earl of Sandwich.
The word 'pyjamas' came into English from Persian and Hindustani.
The # symbol is also called an octothorpe.
'Strengths' is a long English word with only one vowel.
'Bookkeeper' has three double letters in a row.
'Queue' sounds the same even if you take away its last four letters.
'Facetious' contains all five vowels in alphabetical order.
There is no symbol for zero in Roman numerals.
'Forty' is the only number whose letters are in alphabetical order.
A googol is 1 followed by 100 zeros.
Multiply any counting number (1, 2, 3...) by 9 and keep adding the answer's digits: you always end with 9.
A shuffled deck of cards is very likely in an order that has never existed before in history.
In a group of just 23 people, there is a better than even chance that two share a birthday.
A circle has an infinite number of lines of symmetry.
Bees build hexagon-shaped cells because they hold the most honey using the least wax.
The digits of pi go on forever without repeating.
There are more possible games of chess than there are atoms in the observable Universe.
In traditional kabaddi, a raider keeps chanting 'kabaddi, kabaddi' in a single breath during a raid.
Chillies taste hot because of capsaicin. Birds can't feel this heat, so they happily eat chillies.
A cucumber is about 95% water.
A watermelon is about 92% water.
After water, tea is the most popular drink in the world.
You blink about 15 to 20 times every minute.
You are about 1 cm taller in the morning than at night.
Your stomach uses hydrochloric acid, a very strong acid, to help digest food.
Bones are alive. They grow, heal and keep rebuilding themselves.
Your left lung is a little smaller than your right lung, to make room for your heart.
Your baby teeth started forming before you were born.
A red blood cell lives for about 120 days.
Smells are very strongly linked to memories.
Earthworms breathe through their skin.
When some plants are attacked by insects, they release chemicals that warn nearby plants.
Mushrooms are more closely related to animals than to plants.
One of the largest living things on Earth is a honey fungus in Oregon, USA, spreading underground for kilometres.
The coconut crab can crack open coconuts with its claws.
The platypus is a mammal that lays eggs.
A platypus glows blue-green under ultraviolet light.
A cockroach can live for about a week without its head.
The cooling design of termite mounds inspired a building in Zimbabwe that stays cool with little air-conditioning.
The nose of Japan's bullet train was redesigned to copy the beak of a kingfisher, making it quieter.
Geckos can walk up glass because of millions of tiny hairs on their toes.
Lotus leaves clean themselves: water rolls off in drops and carries dirt away.
The crack of a whip is a tiny sonic boom: its tip moves faster than sound.
A rainbow is really a full circle. From the ground we usually see only the top half.
Snowflakes usually have six sides or six arms.
The sky is blue because air scatters blue sunlight more than red.
Sunsets look red and orange because sunlight travels through more air when the Sun is low.
A fluffy cumulus cloud can weigh hundreds of tonnes.
Falling raindrops are shaped more like hamburger buns than teardrops.
Fog is just a cloud that is touching the ground.
Napoleon was not unusually short. He was about average height for his time.
Vikings did not really wear horned helmets in battle.
The shortest war in history, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted less than an hour.
The Eiffel Tower was meant to stand for only 20 years.
The Statue of Liberty is green because its copper skin has reacted with the air.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa leans because it was built on soft ground.
You can see the International Space Station from Earth without a telescope. It looks like a fast-moving star.
The International Space Station travels at about 28,000 km per hour.
An octopus can taste things by touching them with its suckers.
Bats are not blind. Many see quite well and also use echoes to find their way.
Goldfish do not have three-second memories. They can remember things for months.
Bulls don't get angry at the colour red. They react to the movement of the cape.
Camels have three eyelids to protect their eyes from sand.
Elephants can sense rumbles through the ground with their feet.
A giraffe's tongue is dark bluish-black and can be about 45 cm long.
Hippos make an oily reddish liquid on their skin that works like sunscreen.
A woodpecker's long tongue wraps around the back of its skull.
Sloths can hold their breath under water for up to 40 minutes.
Pigeons carried important messages during wars, and some were given medals.
An ostrich can run at about 70 km per hour.
A rhinoceros horn is made of keratin, the same material as your hair and nails.
Clownfish are all born male. Some later change to female.
Some sharks must keep swimming to push water over their gills and breathe.
A tiny jellyfish called Turritopsis dohrnii can turn itself back into a young stage.
Ancient relatives of dragonflies had wings about 70 cm across.
Birds are living dinosaurs.
Tyrannosaurus rex lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
The word 'dinosaur' means 'terrible lizard'.
Dinosaur fossils and eggs have been found at Balasinor in Gujarat.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Neptune has the fastest winds in the Solar System, over 2,000 km per hour.
Olympus Mons, a volcano on Mars, is about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.
Jupiter's moon Europa may have a huge salty ocean under its icy surface.
Saturn is light enough that, in a giant enough bathtub, it would float.
In a honeycomb, the walls of each six-sided cell meet at angles of 120 degrees.
The heart of a blue whale can weigh around 180 kg.
Water expands when it freezes. That is why ice floats and why a full bottle of water can crack in the freezer.
An adult human has 206 bones, and more than half are in the hands and feet.
Your nose and ears contain cartilage, not bone.
Hot air balloons float because hot air is lighter than the cooler air around it.
A bolt of lightning is only a few centimetres wide, but it can be kilometres long.
Mawsynram in Meghalaya gets more rain in a year than almost anywhere else on Earth.
India's Kumbh Mela is so huge that its giant tent city can be seen clearly in satellite pictures.
The game of polo was played in Manipur centuries ago, and British officers learned it there.
The Chola emperor Rajendra Chola I sent ships all the way to South-East Asia.
Zero was first treated as a number with its own rules by Indian mathematicians.
Indians in the Indus Valley used standard weights shaped like cubes, over 4,000 years ago.
The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha was built in the shape of a giant chariot with 24 carved stone wheels.
Some butterflies drink the tears of turtles to get salt.
A group of crows is called a 'murder', and a group of owls a 'parliament'.
Sea otters have the thickest fur of any animal.
Octopuses have three hearts.
Venus is the hottest planet, even hotter than Mercury.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach us, so we see the Sun as it was 8 minutes ago.
Honeybees beat their wings about 200 times every second. That is what makes their buzz.
Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards.
Owls can't roll their eyes. They turn their whole heads instead.

bites.x: Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram touched down on 23 August 2023.

bites.q: Why does the Moon shine at night?
bites.x: The Moon has no light of its own. It reflects light from the Sun.

bites.q: Which planet from the Sun is Earth?
bites.x: Mercury is first, Venus second and Earth third.
